A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreeFuse by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including v1's image-only appendix pages.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 2, component ablations, and a 225-image LoRA layer-removal analysis.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, quantitative ablations, mask-localization experiments, user preferences, and inference-latency measurements.

M1.justification: V1 uses attention-sink filtering, top-1% self-attention aggregation, and SLIC superpixel voting before masking LoRA outputs. V2 introduces discriminative concept scores and latent-similarity propagation through FreeFuseAttn, background competition, morphological and iterative mask refinement, an adapter-disabled extraction pass, and attention-bias guidance (Section 3; Appendix B). These substantially change inference despite retaining spatially restricted LoRA outputs.

E1.justification: V1's main benchmark evaluates pairwise interactions among five characters. V2 evaluates four-character scenes and character-object interactions using ten character and five object LoRAs, substantially expanding anime, 3D, object, and interaction coverage (Section 4.1; Appendix C). Figure 1 also adds generation scenarios incorporating spatial guidance, reference adapters, and style LoRAs.

E2.justification: V1 Table 2 compares LoRA Merge, ZipLoRA, OMG, Mix-of-Show, and CLoRA. V2 Table 1 instead compares LoRAShop, Multi-IP-Adapter, Multi-Redux, OmniGen, and UMO. Older baselines remain in the SDXL qualitative comparison, which adds Orthogonal Adaptation (Figure 9). New localization comparisons evaluate SP-Attn and ConceptAttn variants.

E3.justification: The main evaluation changes from 5,000 images per method with matched character-LoRA training to 470 images across new stress tests using public checkpoints. V2 adds DINOv2, CLIP-I/T, ArcFace, and HPSv2, while removing Gemini scoring and best-of-ten evaluation. It introduces SAM3-referenced localization, blinded preference ranking, and defined latency protocols. Reported FLUX mask extraction changes from step 6/block 17 to step 5/the last double-stream block.

E4.justification: V1's qualitative pipeline ablation and FF/V layer-removal study give way to quantitative cross-attention, post-processing, and attention-bias ablations in v2 Table 2. V2 additionally investigates prompt descriptiveness, extraction timesteps and layers, attention locality, localization accuracy, SDXL transfer, and runtime scaling (Figures 3–4; Appendices A, B, and F).

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports ten seeds, 42–51, per prompt; v2 omits corresponding seed and repetition information for its new benchmark. V2 Figures 4 and 8 introduce shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning. Neither version reports formal significance tests; v2's assertion that its sample count ensures statistical significance supplies no such test.

E6.justification: V1's average/best-of-ten result matrix is replaced by v2's new benchmark, alongside added ablation, localization, preference, and latency results. In v2 Table 1, FreeFuse leads LVFace, 0.2534 versus LoRAShop's 0.2350, but UMO exceeds its object DINOv3, 0.6884 versus 0.6804, and HPSv3, 8.756 versus 8.279. These are different-condition results, not direct performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: V1's derivation invokes small query/key perturbations, FF/V dominance, and approximate equivalence to individual-LoRA inference (Section 3.2). V2 removes that derivation and uses per-token locality and exclusivity to argue stronger isolation (Section 3.1). It also introduces substantive mathematical definitions for discriminative scores, latent propagation, and iterative routing, replacing the earlier mask-construction formulation.

C1.justification: Training-free automatic LoRA fusion remains central, but v2 elevates FreeFuseAttn's superiority over alternative localization mechanisms and compatibility with ControlNet, reference adapters, and style LoRAs into explicit core contributions. Its abstract and introduction strengthen v1's approximate-preservation argument into a sufficient-condition claim for conflict mitigation, while the conclusion claims elimination of feature leakage.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving semantic symmetry, descriptive prompts, temporal/layer alignment, and bias-guided semantic isolation. V1's explanation of occasional mask misalignment and its explicit failure caveat as LoRA counts increase are removed. V2 instead emphasizes computational overhead and scalability, and qualifies SDXL results by the backbone's weaker prompt adherence and spatial capabilities.

D1.justification: V2 replaces v1's Diffusers/Aitoolkit training description with public-checkpoint catalogs and revised prompts, and documents SDXL integration and router hyperparameters, including kernel size 2, 15 iterations, and momentum 0.2. Appendix F defines timing boundaries and resolution on the retained L20 hardware. An explicit code-availability statement replaces the project-page link; these access statements were assessed only as reported in the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 removes the LLM-oriented LoRA-merging discussion and substantially expands positioning against newer fusion and unified-generation methods, including LoRAShop, Orthogonal Adaptation, LoRACLR, OmniGen, and UMO. It also adds extensive grounding in diffusion-model segmentation and attention research, including ConceptAttention, SPDiffusion, and DAAM, redefining the context for its localization contribution.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and substantial portions of the scientific narrative are rewritten. V1's separate Analysis and Method sections become a unified Methodology section. Limitations receive a standalone section, and the appendices are extensively reorganized around architectural transfer, post-processing, experimental materials, user evaluation, and computational cost.

P2.justification: The teaser and pipeline are redesigned, the feature-checklist table disappears, and the main results table is reorganized into character, object, face, aesthetic, and preference groups. V2 adds quantitative ablation and latency tables, locality heatmaps, localization curves, and checkpoint catalogs. The extensive v1 gallery is replaced by new displays, while some older baseline examples reappear in the revised SDXL comparison.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central empirical case by introducing a FLUX-based LoRAShop comparison, quantitative pipeline ablations, and measured locality/localization evidence. These address v1's backbone-confounded competing-method comparisons and qualitative-only pipeline ablations. Broader interaction tests and implementation documentation further support applicability. Lost seed disclosure, unspecified user-study sample size, undefined plot bands, and stronger isolation language weaken transparency and qualification, but the improved experimental support provides a substantial net quality gain.
